timing_analysis: CPU execute grows 3.322 s (340 cells) -> 11.848 s (550) -> 75.771 s (1074) while live vertices go 353/558/1089 and carrier edges 1004/1611/3186. In _sweep_tree the visit body runs once per mesh vertex (jax.lax.fori_loop over vertex_count, line 289) and each visit rebuilds full-mesh pairwise structures: _roots pointer-jumps over all vertices (line 216), the repeated-root collision mask builds an edge_count x edge_count boolean comparison (lines 225-234), and _append_edges rescans all edges for duplicates on each of its edge_count appends (lines 97-105). The per-visit cost is therefore O(V + E^2), so the sweep is O(V*E^2): between 340 and 1074 V grows 3.1x and E 3.17x for a predicted ~30x against a measured 22.8x (550->1074: predicted 7.25x, measured 6.4x). This growth is NOT inherent to contour trees, which admit near-linear O(V alpha(V)) algorithms; it is an implementation choice driven by fixed-shape jit/vmap traceability (dense repeated rescans instead of a per-vertex incident-edge gather and a single-pass union-find). A later node should move the pairwise root-collision test to the incident edges of the swept vertex and the duplicate scan to a run-local structure.
